title: Operational assurance framing for sales
content:
Purpose:
This note is a compact, operationally-focused messaging brief for AEs/SEs and CSEs to use when customers raise compliance, data residency, or audit-log questions. Aim is to translate technical controls into purchase-facing assurances and evidence mapping. Keep this short enough to carry in a sales call and detailed enough to attach to a proposal.

Audience:
- Revenue-facing reps (AEs, SEs)
- Solutions/Technical pre-sales (CSEs)
- Customer procurement/security reviewers (secondary)

Status / scope:
- Draft: internal playbook and suggested language.
- Covers SOC2, ISO 27001, and HIPAA as the three most common asks.
- Emphasis on audit-log transparency, evidence availability, and contract language for data handling.
- Not a replacement for security team responses; always loop in Security for deep-dive requests or bespoke contract redlines.

TL;DR messages (elevator):
- "Redwood Inference operates a production-first platform with third-party validated controls (SOC2 Type II) and ISO-aligned practices — we can map any audit question to tangible artifacts (policy, config, or log extracts)."
- "For regulated workloads we offer Private deployments (VPC/on-prem) and contractual commitments (BAA) to meet HIPAA requirements; our hosted stack supports strong segregation and key management integrations."
- "Audit logs are retained on a per-customer basis per contract; we provide structured, queryable exports and can onboard customers to our long-term retention add-on for compliance reviews."

Core capability claims (short):
- SOC2: Type II (controls over time), independent auditor report available for review under NDA. Controls cover change management, access, incident response, and logging.
- ISO: Practices aligned to ISO 27001 controls; certificate and scope available on request (sales evidence package).
- HIPAA: We sign BAAs and offer Private deployments for PHI; hosted offering can be configured with customer-managed keys and restricted personnel access.
- Audit logs: token-level request traces, model/version identifiers, route and region metadata, user/role attribution (where available), and sampling-friendly KV cache traces for repro.
- Data handling: configurable retention, optional customer KMS (bring-your-own-keys), encryption at-rest/in-transit, and soft-delete vs. hard-delete semantics by route.

Suggested audit-log language to use in proposals and inbound queries:
- "Redwood provides cryptographically verifiable request audit trails that include: timestamp, request ID, model/version, route, region, and the token-level usage metrics required for operational review. These logs are retained according to the contracted retention policy and can be delivered as CSV/JSON exports or queried via our secure audit API.
"
- "For customers requiring longer retention or immutable retention chains, Redwood offers a retention add-on with append-only storage and WORM-like policies; see attached evidence pack for implementation details."

Evidence mapping (what we can produce quickly):
- Auditor report (SOC2 Type II summary) — available under NDA.
- Control narratives: access control matrix, change control runbooks, incident response tabletop summary — 2–3 page artifacts.
- Config snapshots: IAM role mappings for services, network CIDR lists, VPC peering diagrams (for Private deployments).
- Sample audit-log extract: sanitized CSV for a 30-day window showing request IDs, timestamps, and model versions.
- Key management proof: KMS integration screenshots and KMS policy snippets.

Competitive contrast (what we emphasize vs. common alternatives):
- Big cloud providers: offer raw infra logs but not inference-aware audit semantics (model/version + prompt metadata). We can provide inference-specific traces that materially shorten incident forensics.
- LLM APIs focused on convenience: may lack enterprise-grade retention SLAs or BAA options; highlight Redwood’s Private option + contractual controls.
- Self-hosted inference vendors: customers get more control but pay heavy ops cost; Redwood sells predictable compliance evidence + optional managed private with lower operational burden.

Customer-facing scripts and snippets (quick copy for reps):
- Initial ask response: "Great question — we have a SOC2 Type II report and an ISO-aligned program. For audit needs we map any audit question to artifacts (policy, config, logs). I can share the SOC2 summary under NDA and pull a sample audit-log extract for your risk team — who should I share that with?"
- HIPAA / PHI escalation: "We support HIPAA customers via our Private deployment or via hosted with a signed BAA and customer KMS. We can put together a short runbook on how we segment production environments and handle PHI in transit and at rest."
- When asked about log integrity: "We provide immutable-style retention options and append-only export packages for regulatory review. If your compliance team needs chain-of-custody we can coordinate Security to provide the certifying artifacts."

Common objections and rebuttals:
- "We need cryptographic non-repudiation": "We offer signed export bundles and can discuss integration with your SIEM for ingestion; for the highest assurance we recommend our retention add-on with immutable storage policies."
- "We can't share PHI with vendors": "We respect that; Private deployments let you run the inference plane in your VPC/on-prem. For hosted scenarios we offer contractual commitments, strict access controls, and customer-managed keys."
- "We need 7+ years of retention": "We can support extended retention via the long-term retention add-on. We'll propose a retention schedule and export cadence that meets your legal or regulatory requirements."

Contract language - suggested clauses (starter text for legal):
- Data handling clause (simple): "Supplier shall encrypt Customer Data in transit and at rest using industry-standard primitives; Customer may elect to bring its own key management solution. Supplier will not use Customer Data to improve models unless expressly authorized in writing."
- Audit access clause (starter): "Subject to confidentiality obligations and reasonable notice, Supplier will provide Customer or its auditors access to relevant controls artifacts and audit-log extracts necessary to verify Supplier's compliance with this Agreement."
- Retention and export clause: "Supplier will retain audit logs per the retention schedule in Exhibit A and will provide export copies upon Customer request in a machine-readable format with chain-of-custody annotations where applicable."

Quick intake checklist for reps before sending evidence to customer:
- Confirm exact ask: SOC2 summary? Sample log? BAA? Certificate?
- Which environment: hosted vs. dedicated vs. private?
- Desired retention window and format (CSV/JSON/S3 export/secure API)?
- Any requirement for immutable/WORM storage or chain-of-custody?
- Point of contact on customer side (security, procurement, legal) and NDA status.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Confirm scope of our public SOC2 summary (full scope vs. limited controls) — Security to confirm. (Owner: Priya)
- Produce a redacted 30-day sample audit-log extract and a short README on fields included. (Owner: Samir)
- Build a 1-pager BAA FAQ for hosted vs. private flows. (Owner: Tom)
- Template language for retention add-on pricing and SLOs — coordinate with Finance. (Owner: Nora)

Appendix: quick evidence pointers for Security team (for handoff)
- Where to find artifacts: Confluence > SEC > Evidence catalog (linked).
- Preferred format for sample logs: zipped CSV + README + minimal PII redaction.
- When to route to Security: any request for raw access to production telemetry, cryptographic attestation, or bespoke contract changes to data processing terms.

Notes on tone and persona:
- For buyer-facing messages be concrete and operational: "here's the artifact we provide" vs. vague "we have controls".
- Prefer to offer a quick sample immediately — it reduces back-and-forth and builds trust.
- Escalate early: if a customer asks for unusual legal terms (audit rights, onsite audits, or source code escrow), involve Security and Legal immediately.

Next steps / action plan:
- Finalize SOC2 summary scope and store canonical NDA download link (Priya, due 2026-02-28).
- Deliver redacted audit-log sample and attach to sales collateral (Samir, due 2026-03-07).
- Publish a 1-page sales cheat sheet with suggested scripts and contract clauses in the go-to-market folder (Nora, due 2026-03-01).

If something goes sideways on a call: immediate escalation path: SE/AE -> CSE -> Security SLA on urgent: security-oncall@redwood.example (for emergency compliance questions).

---
Draft history: created as a consolidation of recent RFP asks and three post-demo compliance calls (Q4 2025). This is intended to be lightweight and iterated rapidly.

Unresolved: whether we proactively include a short SOC2 summary in initial procurement decks or only share under NDA. Current leaning: under NDA for full report; include a short summary line in public decks.

End of doc.
